$readme: The deletion-claim rule table (#398 / ADR 0013 Amendment 1 / counsel gate CLM-7). ONE table, read by
BOTH censuses: frontend/src/test/marketing-claims.test.ts and
api/CompliDrop.Api.Tests/DeletionClaimCensusTests.cs. Add or broaden a rule HERE, never in one suite —
the ContactEmail precedent (ADR 0038, SharedFixtures/contact-email-cases.json): two hand-maintained
copies of the same table were already unequal at introduction, and round 2 of the #398 review found
the same thing here (5 rules one side, 7 the other, each catching sentences the other missed) while
three records called them 'the same census'.
What is shared is the RULE TABLE. The two censuses still differ in what they WALK, and that is the
point of having two: the frontend walks frontend/src/** plus the repo README; the backend walks
api/CompliDrop.Api/**/*.cs, where a server message lives — invisible to the frontend walk, and where
both of round 2's CONFIRMED majors were found.
Each side compiles these patterns with its OWN engine (JS RegExp / .NET Regex) and folds punctuation
and whitespace with its own normalizer, so 'the two agree' is not asserted from this file — it is
proved on each side by its not-dark test running every `sample` + `alsoCatches` below through its own
engine. A pattern that means different things in the two dialects reddens there.
`sample` is the real retired sentence where one exists; `alsoCatches` pins what a broadening BOUGHT,
so a pattern narrowed back to its historical string reddens instead of going quietly dark. Every rule
needs at least two words, so an identifier (DeleteAccount, DeletedAt, user.account_deleted) cannot
trip one. Patterns are matched case-insensitively.
A display LABEL is a map value, not prose — no rule here can judge one. `user.account_deleted` ->
'Account closed' is asserted directly in both mirrors instead.
retention: nothing in CompliDrop hard-deletes (#398 / ADR 0013 Amendment 1): closing an account scrubs the holder's email + name and soft-deletes the user + org, while the vendors' contact details, the documents, the uploaded blobs, the reminder logs, the Subscription row and the audit trail are all RETAINED — and clearing DeletedAt restores the account, which ADR 0013 names as a BENEFIT

rules.why: ; so "permanently" is false twice over. Broadened past the literal verb the ticket retired: the claim is "permanently" + ANY erasure word, and "permanently removes" is the phrase a new dialog reaches for. Noun forms ride along via `permanent(ly)?`
rules.sample: Permanently deletes your account and organization data. This can't be undone.
alsoCatches: This permanently removes the vendor and everything they sent.
Closing your account triggers permanent deletion of your files.
Confirm to permanently erase this certificate.

rules.why: — nothing is irreversible: the row keeps its DeletedAt tombstone, a document keeps its blob, and support restores an account by clearing DeletedAt. Bare "forever" is deliberately NOT banned — "Free forever", "tracked forever" and "Locked forever" ship, are true, and are about something else entirely
alsoCatches: Once you confirm, this action cannot be reversed.
Once you confirm, this action is not reversible.

rules.why: — every delete path soft-deletes, and DeleteDocument keeps the blob so the document "remains recoverable" (its own comment). Say what the CUSTOMER can't do instead
rules.sample: This removes the document from your records and can't be undone.
alsoCatches: Closing your account cannot be undone.

rules.why: . We delete nothing on closure — say what closure DOES (scrub the holder's name + email, cancel the plan, stop reminders) and what is kept. A modal between "we" and the verb is the MOST natural way to write the promise, and every one of them used to pass. Still scoped to "we <verb> your/all/every…" so the Privacy Policy's honest "…until you ask us to delete them" and "delete what we can" (a REQUEST channel, not a standing promise) stay legal
rules.sample: When you close your account we delete your data.
alsoCatches: We permanently erase all documents you uploaded.
When you close your account we will delete your data.
We may delete all documents you uploaded.
We will then purge everything you sent us.

rules.why: — the passive voice does not make it true; no purge job exists anywhere in the codebase. The tense list is spelled out because the two shapes that actually shipped sit at opposite ends of it: a success toast reporting "has been deleted", and an abort arm reporting the NEGATION, "so your account was not deleted" — which is why the optional `not` is here rather than in a rule of its own
rules.sample: Your data is permanently deleted when you close your account.
alsoCatches: Your documents will be erased once the account closes.
We can't reach billing right now, so your account was not deleted. Please try again later.
Your uploads get wiped when the plan ends.

rules.why: . This is the retired Privacy Policy retention promise verbatim — no purge job exists anywhere in the codebase, so nothing implements it
rules.sample: If you close your account, we delete or de-identify your data within a reasonable period.

rules.why: . A retention SCHEDULE nobody enforces recreates #398's defect in a new sentence — the disposal question is counsel-gate CLM-7, not a copy decision
rules.sample: If you close your account we delete everything you uploaded within 90 days.
alsoCatches: Your uploaded files will be deleted within 90 days.
Closed accounts are purged after 12 months.
